question: Will Haley Stevens win the 2026 Michigan Democratic Primary?
rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the Democratic Primary for United States Senator from Michigan.

If no 2026 Michigan Democratic Senate Primary takes place, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be the first announcement of the results from the Michigan Democratic party, however an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

evidence.excerpt: Tavern Research’s online survey of 2,211 likely Democratic primary voters found Stevens at 42%, El-Sayed at 41%, and 18% unsure, with a reported margin of error of 2.5 percentage points. The poll was conducted the day before and day of the July 7 head-to-head debate. In the survey, 42% thought Stevens could very likely beat Mike Rogers, compared with 37% for El-Sayed.

evidence.publisher: The Detroit News — Melissa Nann Burke and Beth LeBlanc, syndicated by Yahoo
evidence.excerpt: Stevens received 48% support compared with 41% for El-Sayed in a Detroit News/WDIV-TV poll of 500 likely Michigan Democratic primary voters, with about 10% undecided. Among respondents definitely committed to their candidate, Stevens had 34.1% and El-Sayed 33.7%. The article was published July 14, 2026, at 9:01 p.m. UTC.

evidence.publisher: The ELLIS Insight — Jim Ellis, “Close Races to Watch”
evidence.excerpt: A Data for Progress survey for the American Priorities super PAC, conducted July 10–14 among 614 likely Michigan Democratic primary voters, put El-Sayed ahead of Stevens 54%–41%. The same dated analysis reported the contrasting Glengariff survey showing Stevens ahead 48%–41%.

El-Sayed raised nearly $4.6 million between April 1 and June 30, compared with $2.1 million for Stevens. Stevens had about $3.4 million cash on hand compared with $2.7 million for El-Sayed. Outside groups had reported approximately $29 million assisting Stevens, compared with $2.6 million supporting El-Sayed.

Outgoing Sen. Gary Peters endorsed Haley Stevens as his successor on July 13, reversing his earlier intention to remain neutral. Stevens also had endorsements from Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer, Sen. Ruben Gallego, and Sen. Catherine Cortez Masto. El-Sayed had support from Sen. Bernie Sanders and Sen. Chris Van Hollen.
